title: Learner 01 | Day 153: Working increment: Capstone data reliability and scale
body:
## Goal

Working increment: Capstone data reliability and scale

## Implementation contract

**File:** `src/learnforge/specializations/learner_01/experience/rebuild.py`

**Method/unit:** `resume_rebuild`

**Why here:** This is inside your owned AI/ML capability and the named layer. Model/data SDK details stay in adapters, rules in core, and commands/results in experience. It plugs into the same shared project architecture as other capabilities.

**Inputs and expected outputs:** Outbox work resumes; stale updates conflict; derived indexes reconcile; limited caches obey scope and freshness.

**Boundaries:** Keep the change inside the owned capability and preserve accepted behavior.

## Research hints

1. Research **one observed gap in Transactional outbox and event delivery / Reconciliation, cache invalidation, and backfills**. Which rule explains your named unit’s behavior?
2. Search `site:docs.python.org one observed gap in Transactional outbox and event delivery Reconciliation cache invalidation`; use [Python tutorial](https://docs.python.org/3.13/tutorial/) for the relevant small section.
3. Predict one changed input/timing case, run it, and explain each changed value before applying the finding.

## Done

- [ ] Demonstrate this unit’s normal and boundary/failure cases in the working feature.
- [ ] Show the actual run and explain one changed case using concrete values.

**Question of the Day:** For this increment — Add a pluggable local-model option and an image-description draft flow while keeping text-only operation available. — where are the input, state, failure, and output boundaries? Which trade-off did you choose?

**Review with @praadeep28101995:** run the named unit; show actual output and each relevant line’s purpose, before/after values and project contribution.
